Look! A little later I saw many men coming in a company. Among them was a man so tall that he rose above the tower.

2. The six men who had directed the building walked on his right and left. All the workers were with him. Many other glorious men surrounded him.[a] The virgins guarding the tower ran to him and kissed him. They began walking close to him around the tower.

3. He carefully examined the building, feeling each stone. He held a staff and struck each stone built into it three times.[b]

4. When he struck them, some became black as soot. Some were scabby, cracked or chipped. Some were neither white nor black. Others were rough and did not fit with the other stones. Some had many spots. These were the different kinds of unsound stones found in the building.

5. He ordered all these stones removed from the tower and placed beside it. He ordered other stones brought to take their place.

6. The builders asked which mountain they should bring replacement stones from. He told them to bring stones from a nearby field instead of the mountains.[c]

7. They dug up the field and found bright square stones and some round ones. All the stones in that field were brought. The virgins carried them through the gate.

8. The square stones were cut and put in place of those removed. The round ones were hard to cut, and the work went slowly. So they were not put into the building. They were placed beside the tower to be cut and used later, because they were very bright.

Look! A little later I saw many men coming in a company. Among them was a man so tall that he rose above the tower.

2. The six men who had directed the building walked on his right and left. All the workers were with him. Many other glorious men surrounded him.[a] The virgins guarding the tower ran to him and kissed him. They began walking close to him around the tower.

3. He carefully examined the building, feeling each stone. He held a staff and struck each stone built into it three times.[b]

4. When he struck them, some became black as soot. Some became scabby, some cracked, and some chipped. Some became neither white nor black. Others became rough and no longer fit with the other stones. Some developed many spots. These were the different kinds of unsound stones found in the building.

5. He ordered all these stones removed from the tower and placed beside it. He ordered other stones brought to take their place.

6. The builders asked which mountain they should bring replacement stones from. He told them to bring stones from a nearby field instead of the mountains.[c]

7. They dug up the field and found bright square stones and some round ones. All the stones in that field were brought. The virgins carried them through the gate.

8. The square stones were cut and put in place of those removed. The round ones were hard to cut, and the work went slowly. So they were not put into the building. They were placed beside the tower to be cut and used later, because they were very bright.

translation:
  text: 'And look! After a little while I saw a company of many men approaching. In
    their midst was a man so tall that he rose above the tower.


    2. The six men who had directed the building walked with him on his right and
    left. All those who had worked on the building were with him, and many other glorious
    men surrounded him.[a] The virgins guarding the tower ran to him, kissed him,
    and began walking close to him around the tower.


    3. That man examined the building carefully, feeling each stone. Holding a staff
    in his hand, he struck each of the stones built into it three times.[b]


    4. When he struck them, some became black as soot, some scabby, some cracked,
    some chipped, some neither white nor black, some rough and out of keeping with
    the other stones, and some covered with many spots. These were the different kinds
    of stones found unsound in the building.


    5. He ordered all these stones to be removed from the tower and placed beside
    it, and other stones to be brought and put in their place.


    6. The builders asked him from which mountain he wanted stones brought to replace
    them. He did not order them brought from the mountains, but ordered them brought
    from a nearby field.[c]


    7. The field was dug up, and bright square stones were found, along with some
    round ones. All the stones in that field were brought, and the virgins carried
    them through the gate.


    8. The square stones were cut and put in place of those removed. The round stones
    were not put into the building, because they were hard to cut and the work went
    slowly. They were placed beside the tower to be cut and put into the building
    later, for they were very bright.'

  text: 'And look! After a little while I saw a company of many men approaching. In their midst was a
    man so tall that he rose above the tower.


    2. The six men who had directed the building walked with him on his right and left. All those who
    had worked on the building were with him, and many other glorious men surrounded him.[a] The virgins
    guarding the tower ran to him, kissed him, and began walking close to him around the tower.


    3. That man examined the building carefully, feeling each stone. Holding a staff in his hand, he struck
    each of the stones built into it three times.[b]


    4. When he struck them, some became black as soot, some scabby, some cracked, some chipped, some neither
    white nor black, some rough and out of keeping with the other stones, and some covered with many spots.
    These were the different kinds of stones found unsound in the building.


    5. He ordered all these stones to be removed from the tower and placed beside it, and other stones
    to be brought and put in their place.


    6. The builders asked him from which mountain he wanted stones brought to replace them. He did not
    order them brought from the mountains, but ordered them brought from a nearby field.[c]


    7. The field was dug up, and bright square stones were found, along with some round ones. All the
    stones in that field were brought, and the virgins carried them through the gate.


    8. The square stones were cut and put in place of those removed. The round stones were not put into
    the building, because they were hard to cut and the work went slowly. They were placed beside the
    tower to be cut and put into the building later, for they were very bright.'
